title: Data classes
description: What travels on a link, by its rule. A class is named parent or parent.child; a sub-class inherits every rule of its parent and may only tighten its numbers, never change the delivery rule or loosen anything (owner, 2026-11-19, FB-153). Direction and the links a class may travel are attributes of the class, not classes. The numbers of each class (keepalive, deadlines, batch, buffer, expiry) are settled when the transport contract is built (FB-164). Adding a class is one approved change to this list and never a breaking change.

entries.description: Values and events as collected from a source, before curation. Stored and forwarded; replayed with original source times.
Curated records and data products. Relaxed.
Bulk history and backfill. Slow; may be sent in scheduled windows.
Alarms, interlock and safety-related states. Tighter than raw; always sent at once.
Audit records. Always flow upward; never pruned when a buffer fills.
A module's or hub's own state: health, the goodbye, the last will.
Commands: writes to a tag in a process controller (PLC or HMI) that directly affect a process. Never stored; a late one is refused.
Messages to a business system. Delivered and confirmed once and only once; kept while a link is down; does not expire as a command does.
What a hub pushes to set up what is below it: configuration, promoted flows and specs, role assignments, limits. Only the newest matters; kept until delivered.
Credentials, token renewal and revocation. Highest priority; never stored in clear; never replayed.
Live values for screens. The latest value wins; never stored; a late update is dropped.
A question that expects an answer within a deadline: collect on demand, a query. Never stored.
Large objects rather than records: files, model files, flow packages. Sent in pieces, resumable, verified by hash.
